title: Making peace
hookLine: the clans of Mecca nearly fight over who sets the Black Stone, and Muhammad asks for a cloak: sulh, making peace between people
tomorrow: a man went to jail over a tax he refused to pay. why?

lines: A BIKE, A STROLLER, ONE CORNER.
cards: Two neighbors, one stairwell, and a bike and a stroller that both want the same corner. "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God," Jesus said.
Islamic tradition tells of one in Mecca, years before the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, was called as a prophet. The clans of Quraysh are rebuilding the Kaaba.
When it's time to set the Black Stone back in its place, every clan wants that honor for itself. They come close to war. The man chosen to settle it asks for something odd: a cloak.

teach.b: Why a cloak? The clans had agreed that the next man through the gate would judge. It was Muhammad, and they said: here is al-Amin, the trustworthy one; we accept him.
He spreads out the cloak and sets the stone in the middle.
Then he tells each clan to take hold of an edge, and together they lift it up to its place. Only then does he set it in the wall with his own hand. Puzzle solved.
Nobody wins the honor alone, so nobody loses it. Everyone carries the stone. This is Islam's teaching of sulh: making peace between people.
The Quran tells believers that they are brothers, so make peace between your brothers.
And in a hadith in Abu Dawud, the Prophet asks: shall I tell you what is higher in rank than fasting, prayer and charity? Making peace between people.
So a peacemaker, in this teaching, isn't the one who stays out of the fight. It's the one who steps in and finds a way for everyone to hold a corner.

how: Muslims are taught to make peace between quarreling people (islah, sulh), and families and communities may ask a trusted elder to mediate. The story of the Black Stone and the cloak is told from the Prophet's biography.

o: helping both sides set things right

games.q: the stone and the cloak: tap the pairs.

s: Muhammad settled it by placing the stone himself and ignoring the clans
every clan lifted it on the cloak first; only then did he set it in place.
a hadith ranks making peace between people above fasting, prayer and charity
Abu Dawud records the Prophet saying so.
a peacemaker is someone who stays out of other people's conflicts
the story's peacemaker steps in and finds a way for everyone to hold a corner.

games.q: two coworkers both want credit for a project that won the team an award, and your boss asks you to settle it. what would the cloak story suggest?
o: have them present it together, each owning a part
give it to whoever did more; that's only fair
drop the subject so nobody gets upset
games.why: in the story nobody wins the honor alone, so nobody loses it. the peacemaker gives everyone a corner.

practice: Hold your hands out in front of you, palms up, as if you're holding one edge of a cloak with others. Feel the weight shared.
Bring to mind one conflict near you, and for the rest of the sit, look for the corner each person could hold.

wordCard.voice: Making peace: in Islam, sulh, setting things right between people, so that no one carries the stone alone.

orig.note: Arabic: peace, reconciliation; making things right between people.

carryVoice: Your line: peacemaker, the one who hands everyone a corner of the cloak to lift. Day 1731, done.
